item.title: Unraveling vegetation carbon storage using STVisX: a spatiotemporal visual explainable AI framework
item.dc:title: Unraveling vegetation carbon storage using STVisX: a spatiotemporal visual explainable AI framework
item.dc:creator: Chuan Chen Yeming Lao Youjia Liang Yongheng Feng Wen Yi Yongze Song Liqiu Meng a Chair of Cartography and Visual Analytics, Technical University of Munich, Munich, Germanyb Department of Geography, Ghent University, Ghent, Belgiumc School of Resources and Environmental Engineering, Wuhan University of Technology, Wuhan, Chinad Department of Building and Real Estate, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University, Hong Kong, Chinae Key Laboratory of Mine Ecological Effects and Systematic Restoration, Ministry of Natural Resources, Beijing, Chinaf Shaanxi Key Laboratory of Land Reclamation Engineering, Chang’an University, Xi’an, Chinag College of Urban and Environmental Sciences, Peking University, Beijing, Chinah School of Design and the Built Environment, Curtin University, Perth, AustraliaChuan Chen: His research focuses on Governable GeoAI, a GeoAI framework for building interpretable, accountable, and responsible geospatial intelligence. He conceptualized and supervised the entire study, integrated the analytical framework, contributed to the remote sensing data processing and meta-analysis, and wrote and revised the manuscript (Email: chuan.chen@tum.de).Yeming Lao: His research interests focus on GeoAI and ecological sustainability. He led the data processing, contributed to the meta-analysis, spatial analysis, validation and visualization, and wrote and revised the manuscript (Email: yeming.lao@ugent.be).Youjia Liang: His research interests focus on climate-ecological big data and artificial intelligence, and sustainable environmental management. He led the research project, provided the theoretical guidance and supervision, and revised the manuscript (Email: yjliang@whut.edu.cn).Yongheng Feng: His research interests focus on spatial trajectory representation learning and spatiotemporal data mining. He provided strategic supervision and revision of the manuscript (Email: fyheng10@stu.pku.edu.cn).Wen Yi: Her research interests focus on construction health and safety, and sustainable development of urban environments. She provided supervision and revision of the manuscript (Email: wen.yi@polyu.edu.hk).Yongze Song: His research interests focus on GeoAI, spatial statistics, and sustainable infrastructure and Earth-system applications. He provided strategic supervision and detailed revision of the manuscript (Email: yongze.song@curtin.edu.au).Liqiu Meng: Her research interests focus on cartography and visual analytics, geodata integration, spatial cognition, and ethical cartography. She provided strategic supervision, theoretical guidance, and critical revision of the manuscript (Email: liqiu.meng@tum.de).

item.dc:title: Residualized Local Conditional Mutual Information (LCMI): a scalable information-theoretic framework for interpretable and nonlinear spatially varying effect modelling
item.dc:creator: Lingbo Liu a Thrust of Urban Governance and Design, Society Hub, The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou), Guangzhou, Chinab Center for Geographic Analysis, Harvard University, Cambridge, MA, USALingbo Liu is an Assistant Professor in Thrust of Urban Governance and Design at The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou) and a Research Affiliate at Harvard University’s Center for Geographic Analysis. His research focuses on explainable GeoAI, health geography, computational urban science, complex spatial systems, urban robotics, and open-source GIS, with applications in smart city governance and design. As the sole author, he carried out all aspects of this work, from study design and analysis to manuscript preparation and revision.
